title: SKY KART
oneLiner: Race rival planes through stormy skies, grab gadgets, and dive through risky shortcut rings to win the cup.
hook: Choose safe checkpoint lines or risky shortcut rings: shortcuts and boost timing can win a position, but clouds, wind, and collisions can cause a spin-out and a
ramp: Three races form a cup, each with three laps. The opening course teaches steering, altitude changes, crates, and one forgiving shortcut; later courses add stronger crosswinds, tighter ring placement,আ
mechanics: Forward flight is automatic. LEFT/RIGHT steer horizontally, while UP/DOWN move between three readable altitude bands; inputs work immediately when play begins.
Three AI rival planes race the player through overhead courses. The player completes three laps per race and three races per cup.
A collects or uses the currently held item from crates: gust boost, homing balloon, or cloud puff. B activates a 0.7-second personal boost with a 2.7-second default cooldown.
Checkpoint gates must be crossed in course order. Each crossed checkpoint awards 10 points once; missing one makes the next valid route leg readable rather than duplicating score.

Shortcut rings offer a dangerous alternate line. Cleanly crossing one awards 50 points once and advances the route, while clouds, storm balloons, wind, boundaries, and rival contact can disrupt the plane.
Three spin-outs trigger a three-second checkpoint rescue and do not immediately end the race. Rescue returns the plane to the latest checkpoint with clear smoke and invulnerability feedback.
Race placement awards 15, 10, 6, or 3 cup points. After three races, the player wins when their cup total equals or exceeds every rival; otherwise the cup ends in defeat.
Race results advance with A after 1.2 seconds or automatically after six seconds. Resetting a cup clears laps, items, spin-outs, score events, and cup points.
artDirection: Use the skyRacer foundation's bundled overhead plane artwork and HUD. The player plane uses a distinct bright cyan-and-yellow palette, roughly 16x24 pixels, with a wide wing silhouette, blinking engine exhaust, readable banking left/right poses, boost flame, spin-out tumble, and checkpoint-rescue smoke. Rivals use clearly different accent colours and silhouettes. Courses occupy the 256x224 viewport with layered scrolling cloud bands, blue sky gradients, dark storm clouds, visible course boundaries, high-contrast checkpoint gates, shortcut rings, item crates, wind streaks, and hazards kept visually separated from the planes. Reserve the top HUD area for lap, placement, item, boost, and cup information.

preserve: single-player kart-racing structure adapted to an overhead arcade race
automatic forward movement, steering, rivals, item crates, shortcuts, boosts, collisions, checkpoints, laps, and cup progression
change: replace cars and kart presentation with airplanes and aerial courses
retain racing rather than turning the game into flight combat or free-flight simulation

controls.up: Move up one altitude band during active flight
controls.down: Move down one altitude band during active flight
controls.a: Use the held item during active flight; advance race results after the result screen becomes eligible
controls.b: Activate the boost during active flight when its cooldown is ready

lose: The cup is lost after the third race if the player's total cup points are lower than at least one rival.
scoring: Score 10 points per ordered checkpoint, 50 for each clean shortcut ring, plus 15/10/6/3 points for race placement.
